prompt: Slide a fixed-size window across an int array and record the largest value in each position. Complete windowMaxima, returning an empty array when the window does not fit.
explanation: There are values.length - window + 1 positions where a window of that size fits, so the result array is sized from that formula and each slot is filled by scanning the window's own elements for a maximum. Seeding the running maximum with the window's first element (instead of 0) is what keeps all-negative arrays correct. The guard for window sizes that do not fit has to come first, otherwise the length formula would produce a negative size.
hints: The result has values.length - window + 1 entries -- reject window sizes that would make that zero or negative before you allocate anything.
An outer loop picks the window start; an inner loop walks the window's own elements looking for the biggest one.
Start the running maximum at the first element of the window rather than at 0, or arrays made entirely of negative numbers will give the wrong answer.
